A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Uni-Instruct work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison. v2 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR10 and ImageNet64 generation experiments, component ablations, and text-to-3D results, including Tables 1–4 and 7.

after.justification: v2 retains those original image-generation, ablation, and text-to-3D results.

M1.justification: The training losses, model components, and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. The terminal-divergence term added to the theoretical identity is explicitly omitted under a stated assumption, rather than incorporated into the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate conditional and unconditional CIFAR10 generation, conditional ImageNet64 generation, and the same text-to-3D scenarios using NeRF and mesh representations. No evaluated coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 1–3 and 7. The 3D comparison retains DreamFusion, Fantasia3D, and ProlificDreamer in their corresponding backbone settings.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain the same teacher models, initialization and training schedules, evaluation metrics, and 3D refinement procedures. The checklist does not establish a revised experimental design.

E4.justification: Table 4 retains the divergence, GAN-loss, and SiD-initialization ablations. The supplementary divergence analyses and 3D examples are also unchanged; no new robustness or sensitivity analysis appears.

E5.justification: The new checklist states that the random seed was fixed and explicitly explains that error bars were omitted because of computational overhead. These are new disclosures; no seed value, run count, uncertainty estimate, or additional runs are reported.

E6.justification: Numerical tables and sample images are unchanged, but reported result attribution changes. The introduction reassigns CIFAR10 FID 1.46 from unconditional to conditional generation, and Figure 9 relabels its existing samples from Forward-KL to Jeffrey-KL. These reporting changes do not establish new experimental performance.

T1.justification: Equation 3.2 adds the terminal term D_f(q_T || p_theta,T), followed by an explicit assumption that it vanishes. Appendix A.1 corrects the time-dependent divergence in Equation A.9 and adds the integrated identity A.10. Section 3.3 also moves g(t)^2 inside the time integral. These are targeted corrections to the existing theory.

C1.justification: The principal unification, tractable-loss, and generation-performance contributions remain. However, the introduction changes its 1.46 FID claim to conditional CIFAR10, conflicting with the unchanged abstract and Tables 1 and 3, which report 1.46 unconditional and 1.38 conditional.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies subsequent theoretical use by assuming zero terminal divergence and newly acknowledges the computational reason for omitting error bars. Existing explanations of mode coverage, instability, discriminator overhead, and slow convergence remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The checklist newly states that code or anonymized assets accompany the submission and promises a later public code release. Neither PDF contains those attachments, so actual availability cannot be verified. Existing implementation details and hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction now specifically credits Diff-Instruct's application to 3D experiments as inspiration, whereas v1 mentions Diff-Instruct generally. This is a limited attribution refinement; the bibliography, related-work section, and broader research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 appends a NeurIPS checklist and makes localized introduction and theoretical-explanation edits. The main narrative and organization of Appendices A–G are retained without extensive rewriting or restructuring.

P2.justification: Figure 9's caption changes from Forward-KL to Jeffrey-KL while its image panel remains identical. Other changes comprise local equation and text reflow and the appended checklist; existing figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Restoring the terminal-divergence term and correcting the associated derivation modestly improve mathematical accuracy and make the required assumption explicit. These gains outweigh the limited new CIFAR10 attribution error in the introduction. Experimental evidence is unchanged, and the checklist adds only limited reproducibility disclosure, so the overall improvement is modest.
